title: Security: CVE-2021-4279 fix (3.1.1) is incomplete - bare `constructor` segment is still reachable
fix(core): validate primitive json documents
body:
## Summary

Validating a patch against a falsy JSON document currently skips document validation, and applying a child operation with validation enabled can throw a raw TypeError. Validate supplied documents even when they are falsy, and reject child operations on primitive documents with a JsonPatchError while preserving root add, replace, and test operations.

Fixes #340.

## Breaking changes

None.

## Testing

- Added regressions for child add/replace and valid root operations on `0`, `false`, `""`, and `null`.
- Confirmed the new regressions fail on the base implementation (8 failing specs).
- `npm test`: 227 core specs, 83 duplex specs, 1 CommonJS spec, and 3 Webpack import specs pass; TypeScript typing checks pass.
- `npm run build` passes.
- Tests/build ran with Node 24.19.0 and `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider` for Webpack 4. Source was copied to an isolated temporary directory to prevent the old TypeScript compiler from discovering unrelated ancestor type declarations. The repository configuration and test scripts were unchanged.
- Native core benchmarks completed on base and head. The full `npm run bench` then fails in the duplex benchmark because `jsdom` is not declared/installed; the same failure occurs on base and head. No performance improvement is claimed.
- Manual check: `validate([{op: "add", path: "/x", value: 1}], 0)` returns a structured validation error; root replacement of `0` remains valid.
- Browser/device matrix was not run.

Prepared with assistance from OpenAI Codex.

title: Validation is skipped for falsy documents (0, false, "") and then fails with a raw TypeError
generate() returns duplicate root replace patches and doesn't update the mirror after a toJSON type change
Removing a non-index array property via a remove op splices the wrong element
body:
Hi — found this while testing patch application on arrays that carry extra properties.

`arrOps.add` handles non-integer keys (`arr[i] = value`), but `arrOps.remove` always calls `splice`, so removing a property from an array quietly removes the element at index 0 instead and leaves the property in place:

```js
const doc = { arr: [1, 2, 3] };
doc.arr.foo = "bar";

applyOperation(doc, { op: "remove", path: "/arr/foo" }, false);

doc.arr;      // [2, 3]   expected [1, 2, 3]
doc.arr.foo;  // "bar"    expected undefined
```

Not sure a non-index token on an array is even a valid pointer per RFC 6901, but since `add` supports it, `remove` probably should too — or it should throw a JsonPatchError instead of silently removing a different element.

Seen on 3.1.1 (9d313ac), `src/core.ts`.

Thanks!
